questions.question: In the lesson's canonical failure mode, why does the automation demo work but production fail a week later?
options: The model was retrained on stale data between demo and launch
The demo only covers the curated examples the team chose, and production silently fails on the exception cases nobody looked at
The production environment has less compute than the demo environment
The manual team stopped reviewing outputs once headcount was reduced
questions.explanation: The twenty curated demo examples hide the 8% of cases — multi-currency invoices, API-created tickets, non-standard clause ordering — that the team never examined. By the time the silent failures surface, the fallback (the manual team) is often already gone.

questions.question: Which of the four automation-readiness inputs specifically sets the accuracy floor the AI must clear?
options: Output sensitivity
Volume and variance profile
Manual process error rate
Exception map
questions.explanation: The manual process error rate is the baseline the AI has to beat — it also reveals whether 'automation' is really just papering over a process defect that has a cheaper fix than a model.

questions.question: At the 'High' output-sensitivity level, what does the lesson say the automation posture should be?
options: Automate immediately with lightweight monitoring
Automate with a sampling-based human review layer
Human-in-the-loop on every decision, or automation is premature
Delay automation until volume data covers two full years
questions.explanation: High sensitivity means a wrong output has financial, legal, or reputational consequences that survive detection — the lesson's table maps that directly to full human-in-the-loop review, not sampling-based checks.

questions.question: Why does the lesson call it circular to use a model to decide whether a process is ready to automate, and then use that analysis to justify deploying the model?
options: Because models cannot read structured SOPs at all
Because the readiness judgment and the deployment justification would both rest on the same unverified model output, with no independent ground truth
Because ISO/IEC 42001 explicitly prohibits using AI in the assessment phase
Because it doubles the compute cost of the assessment
questions.explanation: If the same model both generates the readiness hypothesis and gets deployed on the strength of it, nothing independent has validated the process. The lesson calls a human audit of a sample the only non-circular baseline.

questions.question: Why does skipping this lesson's readiness gate make a Phase 17 · 20 shadow deployment meaningless?
options: Shadow deployments require GPU quota that only the readiness gate can allocate
A shadow comparison needs a defined baseline of 'correct,' which this lesson's exception map and error-rate measurement establish
Phase 17 · 20 cannot run without a signed scope contract from Phase 14 · 36
Shadow mode only works on processes with fewer than 200 cases per day
questions.explanation: The lesson frames the three-stage sequence explicitly: this lesson establishes what the process does and fails at; without that baseline, a shadow deployment in Phase 17 · 20 has nothing meaningful to compare its outputs against.
